sources: dossier=Required behaviors: 'Claim-producer suite: drives the full claim lifecycle — Open then Commit, Abandon, and Release... plus a retried terminal verb asserting idempotency' (comprehensive-gap-closure) and 'the serialization-9b probe' (corpus-bootstrap), two independent artifact entries; doc=conformance.md:15 pre-edit listed only capabilities/envelope/open/uniformity/split-scope/scopes-conflict; code=claimproducer/runner.go:112-118 runOptionalChecks always appends checkTerminals and checkSerialization9b; cmd/rimsky/conformance.go:160-161 exposes an optional --check-observability/--retention-test-seconds flag not mentioned anywhere in the doc.
note: Dossier corroborates the terminal-verb, idempotency, and serialization-9b checks as intended unconditional battery members; the doc's enumeration was materially incomplete. Fixed by rewriting the claim-producer bullet to enumerate all unconditional checks plus the observability/retention flag (mirroring how the executor bullet already documents its own observability flag).

sources: dossier=Net position: 'Conformance runner logic is an importable shared library... the CLI is a thin wrapper' (repo-reorganization, artifact) plus the general mechanical-check principle (c41b7afe, transcript); doc=conformance.md invariant 1 itself states require-stub-mode 'issues an in-process probe equivalent to the stub-mode probe', which necessarily implies a second copy exists, directly contradicting invariant 2's 'centralized only in the probe subcommand's source'; code=stub-probe signature literals duplicated at executor/runner.go:98,114 (probeStubMode), conformance.go:509-514 (CLI probe subcommand), observability_check.go, and three scenario files.
note: The doc's own invariant 1 and invariant 2 were mutually contradictory (equivalence implies duplication, but invariant 2 claimed single-location centralization), and the architecture position (thin CLI wrapper over a shared library used from multiple call sites) corroborates duplication as the intended/actual shape. Rewrote invariant 2 to state the signature is hard-coded per-site, not centralized.

sources: dossier=none specific to conformance, but design corpus is unambiguous: intent/executor.md 'userdata wire surface (ExecuteRequest.userdata...) collapsed into attributes, no migration shim (2026-05-20, userdata-collapse, artifact)', corroborated independently by intent/attribute.md, intent/validation.md, intent/template.md, intent/inertness.md, and concepts/_retired/userdata.md ('proto:executor.proto::ExecuteRequest.userdata is gone'); doc=conformance.md:14 said 'stub-probe userdata flag'; code=executor.proto:38-45 reserves the userdata field, conformance.go:509-514 sends the flag via ExecuteRequest.Attributes.
note: Multiple independent design-corpus artifacts corroborate that userdata was retired repo-wide in the 2026-05-20 collapse into attributes; the doc used stale vocabulary for a field that no longer exists. Reworded to 'stub-probe flag in the request attributes'.

sources: dossier=silent on this specific wording; doc=conformance.md:14 called the stub-mode probe 'protocol-agnostic'; code=cmd/rimsky/conformance.go:471-544 (runConformanceProbe) builds a genv1.ExecuteRequest and switches on executor Outcome variants exclusively — only --transport (grpc|http) varies, not the target protocol.
note: This is a factual mechanism-description error, not a contested design choice: the probe issues an executor Execute RPC by construction and cannot target a claim-producer or publisher endpoint, so 'protocol-agnostic' misdescribes the shipped mechanism regardless of intent debate. Reworded to name the executor protocol and scope the actual variability (transport) correctly.

sources: dossier=same Required-behaviors entries as row 41 (comprehensive-gap-closure + corpus-bootstrap, artifact, corroborated across two independent artifacts); doc=conformance.md:15; code=claimproducer/runner.go:112-118 runOptionalChecks always appends checkTerminals (terminals.go) and checkSerialization9b (serialization9b.go).
note: Same underlying defect as row 41 (narrower claim, omitting the observability-flag detail); resolved by the same doc edit to the claim-producer battery bullet.

sources: dossier=silent on the DataProcessing battery's exact check list; doc=conformance.md:17 said 'concurrent-writes idempotency' and omitted any begin-candidate idempotency check; code=dataprocessing/runner.go:49 wires checkBeginCandidateIdempotent (line 92-ish: same IdempotencyKey twice must return a byte-equal candidate_handle) and checkConcurrentWrites (8 concurrent begin+commit with distinct keys must yield 8 distinct version_ids — a uniqueness assertion, not idempotency).
note: Verified directly against the runner's own check names and assertions (checkBeginCandidateIdempotent vs checkConcurrentWrites) — an unambiguous doc-vs-mechanism mismatch independent of any contested intent. Rewrote the DataProcessing bullet to name both checks correctly.

sources: dossier=silent on per-role malformed-input coverage; doc=conformance.md:19 said 'per-role happy-path plus malformed-input plus unknown-role checks'; code=validation/runner.go:23-36 Run() — executor case runs checkExecutorHappy + checkExecutorMalformedAttributesSchema + checkExecutorMissingContext + checkUnknownRole, but claim_producer/lifecycle_subscriber/publisher cases run only their happy-path check plus checkUnknownRole.
note: The runner's own role switch is unambiguous: malformed-input coverage exists only for the executor role. Rewrote the Validation-mix-in bullet to scope the malformed-input check to executor only.

sources: dossier=silent; doc=conformance.md:29 said 'the two shared fixture packages' with no identifying detail; code=test/support/claim_producers/{stub,postgres,filesystem}/testfixture (three claim-producer fixture packages) plus test/support/executors/stub/stubtest (a fourth fixture surface).
note: The count 'two' does not match the repo's actual fixture-package inventory and the phrase has no resolvable referent even if the count were right. Dropped the unresolvable count from the Boundaries sentence rather than naming paths (self-containment rule forbids path citations in concept-doc bodies).

sources: dossier=silent on the Adjacent list composition; doc=conformance.md body describes Publisher-protocol conformance (line 18), DataProcessing-mix-in conformance (line 17), Validation-mix-in conformance (line 19), and the lifecycle-subscriber escape hatch (line 29), but the pre-edit Adjacent list named only executor/claim-producer/blob-backend; design corpus=concepts/publisher.md, concepts/data-processing.md, concepts/validation.md, concepts/lifecycle-subscriber.md all exist as concept docs.
note: Self-evident from the doc's own body versus its own Adjacent list — a completeness gap the doc contradicts itself on, not a contested design question. Added publisher, data-processing, validation, and lifecycle-subscriber to Adjacent.

sources: dossier=silent on the exact causal wiring of the stub-mode probe vs the require-stub-mode flag; doc=conformance.md invariant 1 implied the probe runs only when require-stub-mode is set; code=executor/runner.go:57 probeStubMode runs unconditionally on every Run() before opts.RequireStubMode is even consulted (line 58), and lines 74-76 auto-skip any RequiresStub scenario when the probe fails regardless of the flag.
note: The runner's own control flow is unambiguous: the probe is unconditional, the flag only escalates severity, and auto-skip gating happens independent of the flag — none of which the doc stated. Also dropped the undefined 'LLM-calling' qualifier, which no catalog entry defines. Rewrote invariant 1 to state the actual causal shape.
